newsitem.title: FRANCE: French conservative daily embraces Britain's Blair.
newsitem.headline: French conservative daily embraces Britain's Blair.

text.p: The flagship newspaper of the French Right heaped praise on British opposition leader Tony Blair on Friday, saying France's centre-right government could learn from his example in its struggle to bring unemployment down.

Franz-Olivier Giesbert, editor of the pro-government daily Le Figaro, praised Blair for not promising too much in his 10-point "contract with the people", for pledging not to increase income tax and to freeze public spending for two years.

"His programme even goes so far as to proclaim the following credo, which is certainly not politically correct: 'New Labour believes in the flexibility of the labour market for the good of employers and for that of the majority' (of people)," the front-page editorial said.

"French Socialists should read this programme urgently, to banish to the attic their vain dreams and their magic wand for creating 700,000 jobs. Nor would the ruling coalition lose anything from seeking inspiration from New Labour's thinking on 'flexibility'," it said.
Business weekly Valeurs Actuelles splashed the Union Jack on its front cover dedicated to "The English Temptation -- more work, less taxes".

"For many of its potential electors, Blair's 'New Labour' appears to be a more credible alternative...: in fact, we are seeing the rebuilding of a big centre-left electorate, that which ensured the 'historic' Labour victories of 1945 and 1964," it said.

The leftwing Liberation, in its report from London, said Blair had made few concessions to "the left's electorate" and that he unashamedly wanted to increase his party's standing among those disillusioned by Thatcherism.
After two weeks of sparring, Blair delivered Labour's "contract" on Thursday confirming that Labour's old socialist dogma had been dumped.
